# ui::PointerEvent

Header: `winui/core/Input.hpp`.

One mouse / touch / pen event, in window-client DIPs, as delivered to [Element::handle_pointer()](../tree/element.md#handle_pointer) and Window::handle_pointer().

A pen or a finger arrives as mouse events. `device` says which it was and, for a pen, the event carries its pressure, tilt and buttons. A press-and-release pair is what a control counts as a click.

Example: 
```cpp
// In an element of your own: a press and a release inside the bounds is a click.
class ToggleControl : public ui::Element
{
protected:
    bool pointer_override(const ui::PointerEvent& e) override
    {
        if (e.action == ui::PointerAction::Down && e.button == ui::PointerButton::Left)
        {
            pressed_ = true;
            return true;
        }
        if (e.action == ui::PointerAction::Up && pressed_)
        {
            pressed_ = false;
            if (bounds().contains(e.position))
            {
                toggle();
            }
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }

    // The wheel arrives through wheel_override(); return true when the element scrolled.
    bool wheel_override(const ui::PointerEvent& e) override
    {
        offset_ += e.wheel_delta; // positive scrolls down
        return true;
    }

private:
    void toggle();

    bool  pressed_ = false;
    float offset_  = 0.0f;
};
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | `Point` |  | Pointer position in window-client DIPs (the same space as [Element::bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds)). |
| `button` | `PointerButton` | `PointerButton::None` | The button pressed or released; None for Move, Leave and Wheel. |
| `action` | `PointerAction` | `PointerAction::Move` | What happened; defaults to a plain move. |
| `wheel_delta` | `float` | `0.0f` | Valid only for PointerAction::Wheel: the scroll amount in DIPs. Positive scrolls down, so the content moves up, as with a non-inverted wheel. One notch of a standard mouse wheel is a few dozen DIPs. Code that constructs an event converts the platform's wheel units to DIPs first. |
| `modifiers` | `ModifierKeys` |  | The modifier keys held at the time of this event. [TextBox](../controls/text-box.md#uitextbox) extends its selection on Shift+click, and Ctrl+wheel zooms where a plain wheel turn scrolls. |
| `click_count` | `int` | `1` | Valid only for PointerAction::Down: 1 for a plain click, 2/3 for a double-/triple-click. Clicks count as one sequence while they fall within the system's double-click time and distance. [TextBox](../controls/text-box.md#uitextbox) selects a word on a double-click and everything on a triple-click. |
| `horizontal_wheel` | `bool` | `false` | Valid only for PointerAction::Wheel: the turn came from a horizontal wheel or a sideways touchpad swipe, and `wheel_delta` is positive toward the right. A vertical wheel with Shift held stays a vertical turn here. A scroller decides itself whether Shift redirects it. |
| `device` | `PointerDeviceType` | `PointerDeviceType::Mouse` | The device behind the event. A pen's tip and a finger press, move and release as the left button. |
| `pressure` | `float` | `0.5f` | How hard the pen or finger presses, 0..1. 0.5 when the device does not say, which is always the case for the mouse, so pressure-sensitive drawing comes out even. |
| `tilt_x` | `float` | `0.0f` | A pen's tilt along x in degrees, -90..90, positive toward the right; 0 for any other device. |
| `tilt_y` | `float` | `0.0f` | A pen's tilt along y in degrees, -90..90, positive toward the user; 0 for any other device. |
| `eraser` | `bool` | `false` | A pen is erasing: its eraser end is down (the pen is turned over), or its eraser button is held. False for any other device. |
| `barrel_button` | `bool` | `false` | A pen's barrel button is held. With the default pen settings the system turns a press with it held into a right-click, so it shows up mostly on hover moves. |
